issues.legal_issue: A murder conviction may be sustained where reliable evidence and forensic evidence identify the accused as the person who fired the fatal shot.
material_facts: The accused's gun was seized, and ballistic examination established that it had been used in the occurrence.
The prosecution evidence identifying the accused as the shooter was consistent and without material infirmity.
The accused fired a shot that struck the victim in the chest and caused the victim's death.
issues.conclusion: The murder conviction and life sentence were sustained, while the separate conviction for attempted murder with common intention was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: The Court upheld the conviction under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code because the evidence reliably established that the accused fired the fatal shot. The judgment cites no earlier cases for this conclusion.

predicates.appeal_from_conviction_after_acquittal: The accused appealed a conviction entered after a trial court had acquitted the accused.
predicates.weapon_forensically_linked: Forensic examination linked the accused's weapon to the occurrence.
predicates.reliable_evidence_identifies_fatal_shoot: Consistent evidence identified the accused as the person whose shot caused the victim's death.

issues.definition: When an appeal follows a conviction entered after an acquittal, and forensic and reliable evidence link the accused to the fatal shooting, the murder conviction is sustained.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction for causing a death cannot stand where the evidence that an accused used a weapon in the occurrence is doubtful and conflicts with the medical evidence.
material_facts: The prosecution alleged that the accused took another person's gun and shot the victim's arm.
Ballistic examination did not link cartridges from the occurrence to that gun.
The alleged gun's owner was reportedly ill and confined to bed, making his presence at the scene doubtful.
The prosecution's account of the shot conflicted with the location of the entry wound on the victim's arm.
issues.conclusion: The conviction relating to the victim's death was set aside and the trial court's acquittal was maintained.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the doubtful prosecution account and conflict with the medical evidence made the conviction unjustified. Because the trial court had acquitted the accused, the High Court was not justified in reversing that acquittal on this evidence. The relevant conviction was under Sections 302 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code; no earlier cases are cited.

predicates.appeal_from_conviction_after_acquittal: The accused appealed a conviction entered after a trial court had acquitted the accused.
predicates.alleged_weapon_link_doubtful: The evidence that the accused used the alleged weapon was doubtful, including because forensic examination did not connect that weapon to the occurrence.
predicates.wound_evidence_conflicts_with_account: The physical location of the wound was inconsistent with the prosecution's account of how the shot was fired.

issues.definition: When a conviction entered after an acquittal rests on a doubtful weapon link and an account inconsistent with the wound evidence, the conviction is set aside and the acquittal is restored.

issues.legal_issue: An attempted-murder conviction cannot be substituted for an acquittal without assessing whether the evidence concerning the alleged attempt is reliable.
material_facts: The trial court acquitted the accused of the charge concerning alleged shots at two injured witnesses.
The High Court reversed that acquittal and convicted the accused without discussing the prosecution evidence on that part of the occurrence or determining whether it was reliable.
issues.conclusion: The attempted-murder conviction was set aside and the trial court's acquittal was maintained.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that reversal of an acquittal was unjustified where the High Court did not discuss the relevant evidence or determine its reliability. The charge was under Section 307 of the Indian Penal Code. The judgment cites no earlier cases for this application of the principles governing interference with an acquittal.

predicates.appeal_from_conviction_after_acquittal: The accused appealed a conviction entered after a trial court had acquitted the accused.
predicates.appellate_court_reversed_without_reliabi: The appellate court reversed the acquittal without discussing the relevant evidence and deciding whether it was reliable.

issues.definition: When an appellate court convicts on an attempted-murder charge after an acquittal without assessing the relevant evidence's reliability, the conviction is set aside and the acquittal is restored.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction for causing a death cannot stand where the prosecution case against the accused is doubtful and the alleged weapon caused no injury.
material_facts: The prosecution alleged that the accused carried a spear during the occurrence.
No person on the prosecution side had a spear injury.
The Court found the case against the accused sufficiently doubtful, although the High Court had reversed the trial court's acquittal.
issues.conclusion: The convictions were set aside and the trial court's acquittal was maintained.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the doubtful case and absence of any spear injury did not justify the High Court's interference with the trial court's acquittal. The convictions included one under Sections 302 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code; no earlier cases are cited.

predicates.appeal_from_conviction_after_acquittal: The accused appealed a conviction entered after a trial court had acquitted the accused.
predicates.alleged_weapon_caused_no_injury: The prosecution alleged that the accused carried a weapon, but no person on the prosecution side had an injury caused by that weapon.
predicates.prosecution_case_doubtful: The evidence against the accused left the prosecution case sufficiently doubtful.

issues.definition: When a conviction entered after an acquittal rests on a doubtful case and the alleged weapon caused no injury, the conviction is set aside and the acquittal is restored.
